title: News pipeline: multi-source fetch → dedup → Telegram + LLM analysis
description: Personal forex/finance news pipeline. Cron fetches from ForexFactory (XML feed), Yahoo Finance (RSS/yfinance), Bloomberg (GDELT + Google News RSS). Dedup by hash. Fanout: raw → Telegram #raw channel, AND → LLM analyzer (Hermes 4 / Claude Haiku / DeepSeek via OpenAI-compatible API) → structured JSON {sentiment, affected_pairs, time_horizon, confidence, summary} → Telegram #analysis channel. No stealth browser needed for v1. Async fanout so raw post never blocks on LLM.

title: Refactor FF scraper to use faireconomy XML feed (drop Selenium for bulk path)
description: Current ff_calendar_toolkit/scraper.py uses Selenium + Chrome91 UA → slow, detectable, 1000+ req/min. Replace bulk path with HTTP GET on https://nfs.faireconomy.media/ff_calendar_thisweek.xml (also nextweek/lastweek). Parse XML: title, country, date, impact, forecast, previous, actual. Keep timezone cookie logic (fftimezone). Keep Selenium/Playwright as optional --enrich path for High/Medium event detail panels only. Expected ~50x faster, eliminates CF/403 exposure. Files: ff_calendar_toolkit/scraper.py.

title: Add Yahoo Finance news fetcher (RSS + yfinance fallback)
description: Primary: per-ticker RSS https://feeds.finance.yahoo.com/rss/2.0/headline?s=TICKER&region=US&lang=en-US (no auth, ~10-20 items). Fallback: yfinance 1.4+ Ticker(s).get_news() with curl_cffi backend for JA3 stealth + auto crumb/cookie. Configurable ticker list (forex pairs, gold ETFs: GC=F, GLD, USDJPY=X, etc.). Output normalized to common news record schema. New file: ff_calendar_toolkit/sources/yahoo.py.

title: Add Bloomberg headline fetcher via GDELT + Google News RSS
description: Skip direct Bloomberg scraping (Akamai+PX, ToS risk, paywall). Use: (a) Google News RSS query https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=site:bloomberg.com+forex&hl=en-US — returns headlines + URLs. (b) GDELT 2.0 DOC API https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query=domain:bloomberg.com&format=json — free, headlines + tone metadata. Optional: Marketaux/Benzinga if paid sources later wanted. New file: ff_calendar_toolkit/sources/bloomberg.py.

title: Add SQLite dedup layer for cross-source news items
description: All 3 sources will repeat same macro story within minutes. Add seen-table: SHA256 of (normalized title + source-domain) → first_seen_at timestamp. TTL ~7 days, vacuum on startup. Check before fanout. Reuse existing runtime DB if present (see service.py state tracking) or new sqlite file under ./runtime/seen.db. New module: ff_calendar_toolkit/dedup.py.

title: Add LLM analyzer module (Hermes 4 / Claude Haiku / DeepSeek pluggable)
description: Use OpenAI-compatible client (works with OpenRouter, Anthropic-compat, DeepSeek, local vLLM). Model behind MODEL env var; default suggestion: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 (best JSON) or nousresearch/hermes-4-70b. System prompt enforces JSON schema: {sentiment: -1..1, affected_pairs: [str], time_horizon: short|medium|long, confidence: 0..1, summary: str ≤200chars}. response_format={'type':'json_object'}. Skip nousresearch/hermes-agent framework — overkill, replaces existing pipeline. Fire-and-forget from caller (async / thread) so raw Telegram never blocks. Retries with backoff on 429/5xx. New module: ff_calendar_toolkit/analyzer.py.

title: Wire dual Telegram destinations (#raw + #analysis) with rate limiting
description: Extend ff_calendar_toolkit/alerts/notifiers.py: two chat IDs (TELEGRAM_RAW_CHAT_ID, TELEGRAM_ANALYSIS_CHAT_ID). Raw posts emit on fetch+dedup. Analyzed posts emit when LLM returns. Respect Telegram limits: 30 msg/sec global, 1/sec per chat. Use simple token bucket per chat. MarkdownV2 escaping. Optional: forward only confidence>0.7 to analysis channel (env-configurable threshold).
